question: Under RPL Section 441-b, the $185 initial broker license fee is composed of what two distinct amounts?
choice_a: A $155 base fee plus a $30 surcharge
choice_b: A $170 base fee plus a $15 surcharge
choice_c: A $100 base fee plus an $85 surcharge
choice_d: A flat $185 fee with no separate surcharge component
explanation: RPL Section 441-b sets the broker license fee at $155 plus an additional $30 surcharge, together totaling the $185 initial application fee referenced elsewhere in DOS's broker materials.

question: What is the designated purpose of the $30 broker license surcharge (and the parallel $10 salesperson surcharge) imposed under RPL Section 441-b?
choice_a: It funds statewide fair housing testing efforts through an anti-discrimination housing fund
choice_b: It funds county road maintenance in the applicant's home county
choice_c: It is deposited directly into the applicant's own escrow account
choice_d: It funds the DOS employee pension system exclusively
explanation: RPL Section 441-b directs the license surcharges to an anti-discrimination housing fund that supports statewide fair housing testing efforts -- tying license fee revenue directly to fair housing enforcement.
source_note: RPL Article 12-A, Section 441-b (License fees -- fair housing surcharge)

question: Under RPL Section 441-b, what is the total New York real estate salesperson license fee (base fee plus surcharge)?
explanation: RPL Section 441-b sets the salesperson license fee at $55 plus a $10 surcharge, totaling $65 -- notably lower than the $185 total broker license fee, reflecting the different scope of the two license types.

question: Under RPL Section 441-d, what happens to the licenses of salespersons associated with a broker whose own broker license is revoked or suspended?
choice_a: Each associated salesperson's license is automatically suspended, pending a change of association or the expiration of the broker's suspension period
choice_b: Nothing -- associated salespersons keep operating exactly as before under the same broker
choice_c: The salespersons automatically become brokers themselves to keep the office running
choice_d: Only the specific salesperson who caused the broker's discipline loses their license
explanation: RPL Section 441-d provides that revocation or suspension of a broker's license automatically suspends the license of every real estate salesperson associated with that broker, until the salesperson changes association or the broker's suspension period expires.
source_note: RPL Article 12-A, Section 441-d (Salesperson's license suspended by revocation or suspension of employer's license)

question: Under RPL Section 441-d, how is a salesperson's automatic license suspension (triggered by their broker's suspension) legally characterized with respect to that salesperson's association?
choice_a: As a discontinuance of the salesperson's association with the suspended broker
choice_b: As a permanent, non-restorable revocation of the salesperson's license
choice_c: As having no effect on the salesperson's association status at all
choice_d: As an automatic promotion of the salesperson to associate broker
explanation: RPL Section 441-d deems the automatic suspension of a salesperson's license (triggered by the broker's own suspension) to be a discontinuance of that salesperson's association with the suspended broker, which is why the salesperson must then change association to resume active licensure.

question: Under RPL Section 441-e, if DOS proposes to deny a license application, what must DOS do before finalizing the denial?
choice_a: Notify the applicant in writing of the reasons and provide an opportunity to be heard
choice_b: Nothing -- DOS may deny an application silently with no notice at all
choice_c: Automatically refer the matter to the Attorney General for criminal prosecution
choice_d: Publish the denial in a statewide newspaper before notifying the applicant
explanation: RPL Section 441-e requires DOS to notify an applicant in writing of the reasons for a proposed denial and to provide an opportunity to be heard, served personally, by certified mail, or under CPLR procedures -- and, for a salesperson applicant, the associated broker must also receive notice.
source_note: RPL Article 12-A, Section 441-e (Denial of license; complaints; notice of hearing)

question: Under RPL Section 441-e, how many days does an applicant have to request a hearing after receiving notice of a proposed license denial, before the denial becomes final?
explanation: RPL Section 441-e gives an applicant 30 days from notice of a proposed denial to request a hearing; failing to request a hearing within that window makes the denial final.
source_note: RPL Article 12-A, Section 441-e (Denial of license -- 30-day hearing request window)

question: Under RPL Section 441-e, before DOS may revoke or suspend a license or impose a fine or reprimand, how much advance written notice of the charges must the licensee receive before the hearing date?
explanation: RPL Section 441-e requires DOS to provide written notice of the charges at least 10 days before the hearing date in a revocation, suspension, fine, or reprimand proceeding, giving the licensee (or, for a salesperson, the associated broker by certified mail) time to prepare.
source_note: RPL Article 12-A, Section 441-e (10-day pre-hearing notice requirement)

question: Under RPL Section 441-e, does the designated DOS hearing officer have authority to suspend a license on an interim basis while disciplinary proceedings are pending?
choice_a: Yes -- the designated officer may suspend a license pending a hearing, and may issue subpoenas, administer oaths, and take testimony
choice_b: No -- only a court may ever suspend a license, even temporarily
choice_c: No -- DOS has no subpoena or testimony-taking power under any circumstance
choice_d: Yes, but only if the licensee consents in writing to the interim suspension
explanation: RPL Section 441-e grants the designated DOS officer authority to suspend a license pending a hearing, and to issue subpoenas, administer oaths, and take testimony in the course of an investigation or disciplinary proceeding -- powers exercised under CPLR-based subpoena procedures.
source_note: RPL Article 12-A, Section 441-e (interim suspension and investigative powers)

question: Under RPL Section 441-f, how may an applicant, licensee, or other aggrieved person challenge a DOS decision granting, denying, revoking, or suspending a real estate license, or imposing a fine or reprimand?
choice_a: Through a proceeding brought under Article 78 of the CPLR
choice_b: Only through a federal civil rights lawsuit, with no state-court option
choice_c: There is no judicial review available for any DOS licensing decision
choice_d: Only by filing a new license application and hoping for a different outcome
explanation: RPL Section 441-f makes DOS's licensing and disciplinary actions -- granting, refusing, revoking, suspending, fining, or reprimanding -- subject to judicial review through an Article 78 proceeding under the CPLR, brought by the applicant, the affected license holder, or another aggrieved person.

question: Under RPL Section 442-g, a nonresident broker already licensed and regularly engaged in the real estate business in another state may conduct business in New York without maintaining a New York office if:
choice_a: That other state extends reciprocal licensing privileges to New York licensees
choice_b: The broker simply pays double the standard New York license fee
choice_c: The broker is a U.S. citizen, regardless of any other state's licensing rules
choice_d: New York has no such office-waiver provision for any nonresident broker under any circumstance
explanation: RPL Section 442-g allows a nonresident broker regularly engaged in real estate business elsewhere to operate in New York without maintaining a New York office, provided that other state offers reciprocal privileges to New York licensees.

question: Under RPL Section 442-g, New York will recognize an out-of-state license (allowing reciprocal licensure without a New York exam) only if the other state:
choice_a: Requires a written examination and grants licenses to New York licensees without requiring them to take that state's exam
choice_b: Has no licensing requirements of its own at all
choice_c: Charges the exact same license fee as New York
choice_d: Is geographically adjacent to New York State
explanation: Section 442-g's reciprocity mechanism requires the other state to both (a) require a written examination for its own licensees and (b) grant licenses to New York licensees without requiring them to sit for that state's exam -- applicants from non-reciprocal states must instead pass the New York exam.
source_note: RPL Article 12-A, Section 442-g (Nonresident licensees -- reciprocity conditions)

question: Under RPL Section 442-g, what must every nonresident license applicant file with the New York Secretary of State?
choice_a: An irrevocable consent designating the Secretary of State as the applicant's agent for service of legal process
choice_b: A notarized letter from the applicant's home-state governor
choice_c: A New York State income tax return for the prior five years
choice_d: Nothing -- nonresident applicants are exempt from any New York filing requirement
explanation: Section 442-g requires nonresident applicants to file an irrevocable consent designating the New York Secretary of State as their agent for service of process, ensuring nonresident licensees remain subject to New York legal process despite not residing in the state.
source_note: RPL Article 12-A, Section 442-g (Nonresident licensees -- consent to jurisdiction)

question: Under RPL Section 442-g's military spouse provision, DOS must license an applicant who is a member of an armed forces member's household if that applicant:
choice_a: Holds equivalent licensure from another U.S. jurisdiction and meets competency standards
choice_b: Is on active duty themselves, with no other qualification needed
choice_c: Has never previously held any professional license
choice_d: Simply requests a waiver of all licensing requirements
explanation: Section 442-g's military spouse provision requires DOS to license an applicant who is a member of the household of an armed forces member, so long as the applicant holds equivalent real estate licensure from another U.S. jurisdiction and meets applicable competency standards -- easing licensing friction for military families relocating to New York.
source_note: RPL Article 12-A, Section 442-g (Nonresident licensees -- military spouse provision)

question: Under RPL Section 442-i, New York's State Real Estate Board must include a minimum of how many members who are licensed, qualified real estate brokers with at least ten years of New York real estate experience?
explanation: RPL Section 442-i requires the 13-member appointed portion of the State Real Estate Board (alongside the Secretary of State and the Superintendent of Financial Services, who serve by virtue of their office) to include at least five members who are licensed, qualified real estate brokers with ten years of New York real estate experience, with the remaining appointed members serving as public representatives.
source_note: RPL Article 12-A, Section 442-i (State real estate board -- composition)

question: Under RPL Section 442-i, what is the maximum number of years a single individual may serve on the State Real Estate Board over their lifetime, even accounting for reappointment?
choice_c: There is no lifetime limit on service
explanation: Although State Real Estate Board members serve two-year terms and may be reappointed, RPL Section 442-i caps total lifetime service on the board at ten years for any one individual.
source_note: RPL Article 12-A, Section 442-i (State real estate board -- term limits)

question: Under RPL Section 442-k, which specific category of broker regulation is expressly reserved to the exclusive authority of the Secretary of State, rather than the State Real Estate Board's general rulemaking power?
choice_a: Handling of client escrow/trust funds and broker recordkeeping standards
choice_b: Setting the statewide standard commission rate
choice_c: Approving every individual real estate advertisement before publication
choice_d: Selecting the color scheme for DOS pocket cards
explanation: RPL Section 442-k lets the State Real Estate Board promulgate rules affecting brokers and salespersons generally, but expressly carves out client fund handling, property management, and transaction recordkeeping as matters reserved to the exclusive rulemaking authority of the Secretary of State -- reinforcing the Secretary's central role in escrow and recordkeeping oversight found throughout 19 NYCRR Part 175.
source_note: RPL Article 12-A, Section 442-k (Powers and duties of the state real estate board)

question: Under RPL Section 442-k, what must the State Real Estate Board submit annually to the assembly and senate judiciary committees?
choice_a: A report describing complaint types, case status, and resolution timelines
choice_b: A list of every licensed broker's personal home address
choice_c: A projection of the following year's statewide average home sale price
choice_d: Nothing -- the board has no reporting obligation to the legislature
explanation: Section 442-k requires the State Real Estate Board to submit an annual report to the assembly and senate judiciary committees describing the types of complaints received, their status, and how they were resolved -- a legislative oversight mechanism over DOS's real estate disciplinary process.
source_note: RPL Article 12-A, Section 442-k (State real estate board -- annual legislative reporting)
